name: 06-flow-invalid
description: Stale readers. Lane A writes a grain, releases its writer (which deletes the flow, since a reader holds no lock) and recreates it -- a new inode. Lane B shows that a stale reader returns OK with STALE DATA for an index it still holds, reports MXL_ERR_FLOW_INVALID only on a read that would be TOO_EARLY, and that recovery needs every reader reference on the instance dropped, not a new instance: mxlCreateFlowReader hands back a cached reader while any reference remains.

A.note: last writer: makeExclusive succeeds and the flow directory is deleted
same flow id, new file: a new inode is what makes lane B's reader stale

B.note: the SAME pointer as R: getFlowReader caches by flow id and adds a reference
baseline: the 0xAA grain, before anything is deleted
the flow has been deleted and recreated -- and this still returns OK. Compare stamp.write_ns with b3: identical means STALE DATA, silently
one past the stale head: TOO_EARLY triggers the inode check, so this is where MXL_ERR_FLOW_INVALID finally appears
Rdup still holds a reference, so this is the CACHED stale reader, not a new one
the trap: a brand new handle, still MXL_ERR_FLOW_INVALID
refcount 0: NOW the instance forgets the flow
same instance I2, never recreated -- this one really opens the new file
the 0xBB grain: a NEW stamp.write_ns is the proof of recovery
